back: The ordered stages for developing a new information system, from problem identification to maintenance.
Problem identification, feasibility study, analysis, design, development and testing, implementation, (documentation), evaluation, maintenance.
Studies the existing system, finds problems and requirements, and designs and oversees the new system.
Defines the problem, sets the objectives and scope of the new system, and reports whether to do a feasibility study.
+ many people, cheap, anonymous, easy to analyse. − low return, no follow-up, questions may be misunderstood.
+ detailed, follow-up questions, body language. − time-consuming, few people, not anonymous, may hear what the analyst wants.
+ real data, fields, volumes; facts not opinions. − documents may be out of date or confidential; time-consuming.
+ shows what really happens, first-hand. − people act differently when watched; time-consuming; no opinions.
Many people → questionnaire; detail from a few → interview; actual data → record inspection; real procedures → observation.
